thread:
sam: Heads-up — saw a regression on Llama-3-medium serving after yesterday's kernel selector change. 99th latency up ~18% on chat workloads with long histories. Anyone digging in?

anya: Oof. Which kernel landed? selector moved some cases to triton_fused_attn for head_dim=128 right?

sam: Selector prefers fused_attention when head_dim<=128 and seq_len<=1024. We forced it yesterday to avoid fallback to slower flash kernels.

miguel: Can you paste the perf trace? also, which rope_theta/rope_scale are we using for Llama-3-medium? those affect rotary offset math and can change kernel choice.

sam: Perf trace (top hotspots):
```
wall  p50  p95  p99
----  ---- ---- ----
attn_fwd  4.2ms 8.0ms 18.9ms
kv_read   0.9ms 1.8ms 2.4ms
triton_gemm 1.1ms 2.2ms 3.6ms
other    0.8ms 1.0ms 1.3ms
```
Not huge but comparison to last week shows attn_fwd p99 +18%.

anya: What's the kv cache hit pattern? chat workload with prefix caching should avoid recomputing past tokens.

perf-bot: KV cache stats (sample): total_reqs=12.3k, cache_hits=9.1k (74%), avg_prefix_len=420, avg_generation_len=64.

sam: Cache hit looks fine. But noticed we changed continuous-batching heuristic: max_batch_delay from 6ms -> 3ms. That increases small-batch frequency. Could cause kernel mis-utilization.

ben: If batches are smaller we lose GEMM efficiency for triton_gemm and fused_attention. For head_dim=128, fused_attention is optimized, but only at batch*N_heads*seq_len multiples. Missing that leads to lower occupancy.

miguel: Also check RoPE scaling default — Llama-3 uses rope_theta ~10000? If we changed scaling (rope_scale=1.0 -> dynamic) it can change pairing code path used in fused kernel.

sam: Our model config: hidden_size=3584, num_heads=28, head_dim=128, rmsnorm, activation=SiLU, rope_theta=10000, rope_scale=1.0 (default). We didn't change those.

anya: Do we have perf regression correlated to specific sequence length buckets? e.g., seq_len>512 or tails?

perf-bot: Histogram from last 60m:
```
seq_len: bucket(0-128)=12%, 129-512=38%, 513-1024=40%, >1024=10%
p99 latency spike concentrated in 513-1024 bucket
```

sam: That matches. The selector currently picks fused_attention for seq_len<=1024 and flash_attn for >1024. But fused attention implementation we chose has a known slowdown when batch_dim small and seq_dim medium due to suboptimal tiling.

ben: Quick test idea: force the runtime to use flash_attn for the 513-1024 bucket and compare. Might be slower normally but could have better p99 under small-batch regimes.

miguel: Agreed. Also investigate KV packing: we keep KV in separate buffer with stride=hidden_size. If we repack KV into contiguous heads-first layout we can speed memory loads for fused kernel. That change helps when occupancy low.

sam: Running A/B now: route 10% of traffic with flash_attn for head_dim=128, seq_len in [512,1024], and 10% with fused + kv-repack. Will share traces in ~20 min.

infra-bot: Deploy note — canary policy created: model=llama-3-medium, route=seq_512_1024, cohorts=[flash10,kvrpack10,baseline80]. TTL=30m.

anya: While canary runs, check kernel microbenchmarks on target GPU (A100 40GB). I suspect the triton kernel launch overhead dominates at smaller batch sizes. We should log launch_time and compute_time separately.

perf-bot: Microbench results (A100):
```
kernel=fused_attention, batch=1, seq=768, head_dim=128 -> launch=0.12ms, compute=6.1ms, throughput degraded vs batch=4 compute=2.4ms
kernel=flash_attn, batch=1, seq=768, head_dim=128 -> launch=0.15ms, compute=5.0ms
```
So flash_attn compute is lower at small batch. fused has worse compute due to memory pattern.

ben: That explains p99. Selector wrong tradeoff: fused was chosen for theoretical throughput but only wins at larger batch sizes. Our batching heuristic change lowered batch sizes so we need the selector to be aware of effective_batch = batch_size * avg_requests_per_gpu.

sam: Canary update: flash_attn cohort p99 reduced by 22% vs baseline; kvrpack cohort reduced by 15%. Baseline unchanged.

anya: Good. We should implement two fixes: 1) Update kernel selector to consider effective_batch and seq_len jointly (use measured launch+compute model), 2) KV pack path as opt-in pipeline optimization behind a config flag.

miguel: Also add an autosampler that records head_dim * batch * seq and picks kernel by lowest modeled p99 from historical traces. Avoid hard thresholds like head_dim<=128 alone.

ben: Note — any change to KV layout will change memory accounting and eviction behavior. Need to test mem-use under max-concurrency. Add a memory-safety check.

sam: I'll draft a PR with selector change and a feature flag for kv_repack. Targets: revert batching max_delay to 6ms as emergency rollback and land smarter selector in 48h.

infra-bot: Rollback plan created: revert config max_batch_delay -> 6ms for all production shards.

sam: Draft PR: https://repo/pulls/4224 (selector + kv_repack flag). Tests included: microbench, mem-safety, end-to-end chat p99 A/B.

anya: One more item: chat templates. Long system prompts we treat as prefix and cache; but some customers use dynamic system instructions per message. That reduces cache hit and pushes seq_len into mid bucket. We should log whether p99 customers correlate with dynamic system prompts.

perf-bot: Session segmentation: top 5 p99 customers have dynamic_sys_prompt_rate > 60%.

sam: Marking follow-ups: 1) selector model, 2) kv_repack rollout tests, 3) add effective_batch metric, 4) add dynamic_sys_prompt tag to traces. I'll handle 1/3, miguel takes 2, ben handles 4.

miguel: On kv_repack rollout — will stub as runtime flag and add a background converter to avoid OOM spikes.

ben: I'll add logs for rope_theta mismatches between model metadata and loaded config; previously some models shipped with rope_theta=65536 by mistake. That can choose different kernel codepaths.

sam: Nice catch. OK merging rollback now and landing canary fixes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Config rollback executed: max_batch_delay=6ms rolled to 100% in prod.

sam: Postmortem note: small change in batching heuristic + static kernel thresholds caused perf regression. Root causes: 1) selector not accounting for effective_batch; 2) fused_attention non-ideal tiling for small-batch medium-seq; 3) KV layout not optimal for that kernel. Action items above.
